title: Marriage, Divorce, Maintenance and Protection
summary: Maintenance (monthly money to support a family member), divorce, child custody and safety from violence at home, in simple words.
sectionRefs: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Section 144, formerly CrPC 125)
Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005

body.text: Family fights are painful. The law tries to protect the weaker person. This means children, and a husband or wife or parent who depends on others. If you know the basics, you can act without fear.

items: A person who cannot support themselves can ask for a monthly money amount. They can ask their husband or wife. Sometimes they can ask their children or parents.
This rule is in the BNSS (a new criminal law). It applies to all religions.
The court looks at what the person asking needs, and what the person paying can afford.
A marriage is registered under the marriage law that applies to you. Registration makes it much easier to prove.
Divorce can happen if both agree (mutual consent). Or it can happen for special reasons, under the personal law that applies to you.
Either husband or wife can ask for maintenance. But usually it is asked by a wife, children or parents who depend on others.

body.text: Custody of children (who the child lives with)

items: The court decides custody based on what is good for the child. It does not decide by who earns more.
Usually both parents keep the right to visit the child and to be part of the child's life.
Hitting, mental hurt, sexual abuse and taking away money are all covered by the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005.
A woman can ask the court for a protection order (an order to keep her safe), a residence order (the right to stay in the house) and money relief.
You can get help from Protection Officers and the women's helpline 181.

body.text: The rule on maintenance (Section 144 of the BNSS, earlier Section 125 CrPC) is a fast remedy. It is meant to stop a person from becoming very poor. It covers wives, children and parents.
If you or someone at home is in danger right now, call 112 first. Safety comes before any legal step.
Write down what happens in a diary. Keep medical records and any messages. Good records help the court act faster.

practicalSteps: If there is danger right now, call 112. For advice and a safe place to stay, call 181.
For free legal help, contact the District Legal Services Authority.
File the maintenance application before the Magistrate (a judge) where you live.
Keep records of income, expenses, and any threats or bad treatment.
exceptions: Maintenance can be refused if the person asking can support themselves, or has married again, or for some other reasons.
Different communities also have their own separate rules in their personal laws.

faqs.q: Can a man ask for maintenance?
faqs.a: The BNSS rule applies to any person who cannot support themselves. But usually women, children and parents use it.

faqs.q: Does a wife need to prove bad treatment to get maintenance?
faqs.a: No. Maintenance is about not being able to support yourself. It is not about proving bad treatment. Bad treatment matters for other things, like divorce.

sources.label: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 - India Code

misconceptions.fact: Children and parents can ask too. Any person who cannot support themselves can ask.
